az_right_section.blurb: The Right Section is the right-hand end of Granite Mountain, in the high desert northwest of Prescott. It is mostly a trad venue, with a few bolted lines and top-rope options among its two dozen or so climbs. Much of the wall is a blank face rather than cracks, though a few crack lines break it. Grades start around 5.7 and climb through the 5.10s and 5.11s into the low 5.12s, so there is something for moderate leaders and for experts. Expect quiet days and a long uphill walk in from the Granite Basin trailhead.
az_right_section.parking_note: Drive out Iron Springs Road and turn right onto paved Granite Basin Road. It runs about four miles to the Metate day-use lot, where the trail starts. A regular car is fine.

az_gardener_s_wall.blurb: Gardener's Wall is a granite face in the McDowell Mountains on the north side of Scottsdale, tucked just below Tom's Thumb inside the McDowell Sonoran Preserve. It is one of the few multi-pitch walls in the northeast Phoenix area. Most of the roughly two dozen routes are trad, with a handful of bolted lines, and they run from easy terrain up through the 5.10s with a single route in the 5.11s. The popular lines are moderate two-pitch climbs. The walk in is a real hike, so carry plenty of water. It sees fewer people than the thumb itself. Winter and spring are the comfortable seasons, since the rock bakes in summer.

az_lower_looner_land.blurb: Lower Looner Land is a cluster of small pinnacles in the Mine Area of Queen Creek Canyon, above Superior in central Arizona. Nearly all the routes are bolted, with a couple of trad lines and a lone boulder problem. Grades run from easy fifth class through the 5.10s and into the 5.11s, with a solid middle of 5.9 and 5.10. Holds are mostly positive edges with the odd deep pocket, and some are sharp on the fingers. The walk is short, from the little lot at the end of the road. Access near the mine could also change, so check with the local climbers' coalition.
az_lower_looner_land.approach: From the small lot, follow the old dirt road south as it bends west, then continue west up the wash. The pinnacles appear within a few minutes.

az_hackberry_creek.blurb: Hackberry Creek is a stream-side crag in Lower Devil's Canyon, the remote end of Queen Creek country near Oak Flat, east of Superior. The climbing is more trad than sport on volcanic pillars and towers along both banks of the creek, with a waterfall partway up. Grades run from the 5.6 range to the low 5.11s, with most routes between 5.7 and 5.10. Bolts can be sparse even on sport lines, so bring a small rack. The long, rough dirt road keeps traffic light, so expect solitude, but you will need a sturdy vehicle or a walk at the end.
az_hackberry_creek.parking_note: Drive Magma Mine Road beyond Oak Flat, and roughly a mile and a half on take the dirt FR315 to the left, closing the gate after you. Follow it south and then southeast for around two miles into the Hackberry Creek valley. The last quarter mile is rough, so without high clearance park in the small pullout just past the windmill.

az_main_wall_north.blurb: Main Wall North is one sector of Isolation Canyon, a quartzite gorge cut by Pine Creek just outside the town of Pine in the Tonto National Forest. The rock is very hard and coated with lichen, with surprising friction and good edges. Most of the climbs here are trad, with a smaller group of bolted sport lines, and several run to multiple pitches. Grades start near 5.6, with a cluster at 5.8 to 5.9 and the biggest group in the 5.11s. Walls throughout the canyon are near vertical and heavily featured. It is a relaxed, scenic place for a mellow day focused on movement, and the trail in can be hard to follow.

az_atlantis_north_side.blurb: The north side of Atlantis sits in a cleft of Queen Creek Canyon just past the big tunnel on the road east of Superior. Compared with the south side, the rock is steeper and the climbing harder: most routes are bolted, with some trad lines and a boulder problem. Expect a lot of 5.10 and 5.11 with a good number of 5.12s and a few 5.13s, and little at the easy end. The rock is mostly solid, though some loose pieces are normal for this canyon.
